incident: Public documents and world transitions intermittently took several seconds or reached the origin timeout surface.
observedEvidence: Before repair, representative public documents returned X-VII-Edge-Cache-Skip: build_mismatch.
The edge EXPECTED_BUILD referenced 90a45426-e375-4c53-cc48-28a73a2817bf while public application v888 served a80f53ca-0270-c4f2-ad57-2156821fdc89.
After aligning the generation, six representative routes progressed MISS to HIT and warm samples completed in 304-545ms.

A clean browser visit exposed one cold holiday rail before the repaired scheduler had rebuilt its snapshots; after warming, a second clean visit rendered both rails and tab changes completed in 306-620ms.

The retired scheduler read up to 66 public documents every two minutes and previously warmed holiday snapshots and homepage documents concurrently, so it could overload a blocked origin and cache a homepage shell before the verified holiday seed existed.
Several first-document payloads still exceeded 800KB uncompressed, with vacations/north above 1.3MB.

hypotheses.claim: Stale edge generation forced every otherwise-cacheable document to the slow Sites origin.
The remaining cold-route delay is amplified by serializing full catalogs, rails and structured data into initial HTML and Flight.
Images alone caused the document wait.
Concurrent holiday snapshot and homepage warming allowed the cached document to precede its verified seed.
Recurring broad document warming was necessary to keep the slider APIs fast.

prevention: A live edge-generation audit must fail release sign-off when the second exact request is not HIT or when app/cache builds differ.
A ten-minute scheduler warms only five near-date and up to six CMS holiday snapshots with two concurrent reads and a 55-second global deadline.
Recurring public-document warming is disabled; release warming and the edge-generation audit prepare exact document variants once, while R2 demand caching and ahead refresh keep them fast afterward.
The former two-minute 66-document fan-out is guarded by a configuration test and cannot be restored silently.
Payload caps that changed inventory completeness, counts or cheapest-offer semantics were rejected by regression tests and reverted.
Release evidence must include cold, warm, mobile and desktop checks rather than a build-only claim.
